questions.prompt: A pendulum with q measured from the downward vertical is released at rest at q = +60 degrees with no torque and no damping. What is the sign of its initial angular acceleration?
options: Zero, because the velocity is zero at the instant of the release
Negative: it accelerates back toward the downward vertical
Positive: it accelerates away from the vertical, since q is positive
Positive for the first half period only, then it turns negative
questions.explanation: With V = m g l (1 - cos q), the gravity term m g l sin q is positive and the acceleration is -(g/l) sin q: negative, restoring toward q = 0.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg point mass sits 0.2 m from a joint axis. What is its joint inertia m l^2 in kg m^2? Give 2 decimals.
A 1.5 kg tool is held 0.6 m from the joint with the link horizontal (g = 9.81). What joint torque is needed in N m? Give 2 decimals.
For a damped joint, dE/dt = tau*qd - b*qd^2. With tau = 2 N m, qd = 3 rad/s and b = 0.5 N m s/rad, what is dE/dt in W? Give 1 decimal.
You must simulate an undamped pendulum for a long time and care about bounded energy error at low cost per step. Which method is the best fit?
options: Explicit Euler with a large step
Explicit Euler with a small step
No integration; use the small-angle formula only
questions.explanation: Symplectic (semi-implicit) Euler keeps the energy error bounded and costs one force evaluation per step; explicit Euler gains energy, RK4 is accurate but still drifts slowly and costs four evaluations.

questions.prompt: What is the small-angle period of a pendulum with l = 1 m (g = 9.81) in seconds? Give 3 decimals.
A single link has a 2 kg point mass at l = 0.5 m, with the joint angle q measured from the horizontal. What is the gravity torque m g l cos q at q = 60 degrees in N m? Give 3 decimals.
Which statement about the manipulator mass matrix M(q) is correct?
options: It is constant for all configurations of the arm
It is diagonal for any serial arm, so the joints never couple
It can have negative eigenvalues for some poses of the arm
It is symmetric positive definite and varies with the configuration
questions.explanation: M(q) is symmetric positive definite and depends on the configuration (for example on q2 for a 2R arm).

questions.prompt: A joint needs a holding torque tau_j. The gearbox has ratio N (motor turns N times per joint turn) and efficiency eta. What torque must the motor supply?
questions.explanation: The gearbox multiplies torque by N and loses a fraction to inefficiency: tau_m = tau_j / (N eta).

questions.skillLabel: Instability rate of the inverted pendulum
questions.prompt: Near the upright position the deviation of a pendulum grows like exp(sqrt(g/l) t). For l = 0.5 m and g = 9.81, what is the growth rate in 1/s? Give 2 decimals.

questions.skillLabel: Why fixed-gain control fails when the payload changes
questions.prompt: A joint controller tuned with an empty gripper oscillates when the arm carries a heavy payload, and drifts when the arm is stretched out. Use M(q) and g(q) to explain both effects and propose a fix.
rubric: Payload and posture change the effective inertia M(q), so the loop gain/bandwidth and damping change (oscillation)
Gravity torque g(q) acts as a constant-like disturbance that depends on posture and payload, causing steady-state error with a PD law
Proposes gravity compensation / feedforward, computed-torque control using M(q), or an integral term plus gain scheduling
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Explain how you would use energy as a diagnostic for a pendulum simulation, and name two causes of non-conservation that are not model errors.
rubric: Computes E = K + V along the trajectory and checks dE/dt = tau*qd - b*qd^2 (constant for no torque/damping)
Names numerical causes such as integrator type, step size, or round-off, and says to halve the step to see whether the drift scales as expected
Notes that a gravity sign or unit error shows up as a large, step-size independent energy violation
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.skillLabel: Joint torque from the manipulator equation
questions.prompt: A planar 2R arm (angles from the horizontal) has m₁=m₂=2 kg point masses at the link ends, l₁=l₂=1 m, g=10 m/s². At q=(π/4, π/4) with q̇=(2, −1) rad/s and q̈=(3, −1) rad/s², what torque τ₁ (N m) does joint 1 need?
questions.explanation: τ=M(q)q̈+c(q,q̇)+g(q). M₁₁=m₁l₁²+m₂(l₁²+2l₁l₂cos q₂+l₂²)=8.8284, M₁₂=m₂(l₁l₂cos q₂+l₂²)=3.4142, so (Mq̈)₁=8.8284·3−3.4142=23.071. c₁=−m₂l₁l₂ sin q₂(2q̇₁q̇₂+q̇₂²)=−1.4142·(−4+1)=4.243. g₁=(m₁+m₂)g l₁cos q₁+m₂g l₂cos(q₁+q₂)=28.284+0=28.284. Sum τ₁=55.598 N m.

questions.prompt: For the linearised pendulum with ω²=g/l=9.81 s⁻² integrated by explicit Euler with Δt=0.01 s, the energy is multiplied by (1+ω²Δt²) per step. By what factor does the energy grow over 1000 steps (10 s)?
questions.explanation: Explicit Euler maps (x,v) to (x+Δt v, v−Δtω²x); its eigenvalues are 1±iωΔt with modulus² 1+ω²Δt² = 1.000981. Over 1000 steps (1.000981)^1000 = 2.666. The same order as the measured doubling for the nonlinear pendulum of the lesson. For a fixed duration the growth rate per second is about ω²Δt, so halving Δt halves the exponent.

questions.skillLabel: Maximum acceleration with an optimal gear ratio
questions.prompt: A joint has load inertia 0.5 kg m² and motor rotor inertia 2×10⁻⁵ kg m². With ideal gearing the load acceleration is G τ_m/(I_link+G² I_rotor). Maximised over G, what acceleration (rad/s²) results per 1 N m of motor torque?
questions.explanation: d(acc)/dG = τ_m (I_link − G² I_rotor)/(I_link + G² I_rotor)² = 0 gives G*=√(I_link/I_rotor)=158.1, where the reflected rotor inertia equals I_link. Then acc = G* τ_m/(2 I_link) = 158.11·1/(1.0) = 158.11 rad/s² (equivalently 1/(2√(I_link I_rotor))). For comparison G=50 gives only 90.9.
